rounds.comments: Guess the word from its multiple etymologies

clues.text: When used to describe an enclosed plot of multiple buildings it comes from the Malay for "a village." When used to describe making one thing from several, it comes from the French for "arrange"
When used for the end of a sleeve, it comes from the Latin for "head covering." The blow to the head comes from the Swedish for "push"
This derived its meaning of a "puzzle" from the Old English for "conjecture," but it's definition of "perforation" from the old English for "sieve"
As a blemish, it is from the Old English for "mark." For an animal, it comes from the Middle Dutch for "loose earth." For a chemistry counting term it come from the German for "molecule."
For a body of water, it comes from the Norse for "strait." For a noise, it comes from the Latin for "noise." For being uninjured, it comes from the Old English for "health."
